method: isolate true aircraft before combined silhouette
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer and mechanical component reference. Draw this EXACT standalone bomber aircraft as a clean KINETIC_CEL animation design drawing, 1536x1024 landscape, one three-quarter front/top view on plain ivory background. This is the actual bomber component that will later sit across a combined robot's torso. There is NO robot, NO head, NO arms, NO legs in this image.

The single attached aircraft image is the sole STRUCTURAL source. Preserve its unmistakable full broad flying-wing airframe, deep wide center fuselage, big planar swept wing area, front orange wedge nose and single faceted dark glazed central cockpit, low wide dorsal hump aft of the cockpit, paired black upper intakes and two cylindrical underslung engine nacelles. Both wings must have genuinely large triangular planform and wide chord, not thin pointed shoulder armor or linear sticks. Show complete left/right wing tips and their rear trailing-edge panels with ample empty margin; fit the WHOLE aircraft inside the canvas. The mass of the center-body and engine housings must look substantial and load-bearing.

Use orange/ivory/graphite to match the combined robot family: ivory painted leading-edge panels, broad graphite wing surfaces and underframe, orange nose and narrow orange accents. Absolutely no rows of passenger windows, train doors, carriage bodies, separate shoulder cabs or jet fighter sword-wings. Only the ONE central cockpit has glass. The aircraft retains the broad low industrial bomber silhouette of the reference. Do not reinterpret it as a humanoid or a chest plate.

Rendering change only: sophisticated hand-inked mecha animation key art, precise clean planes, crisp hard-edged shadows, flat color areas, restrained panel seams, no photoreal materials, no grain, no cinematic lighting. No electric rings, motion blur, labels or lettering. Geometry and material planes are legible for a low-poly artist.
